original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-projective-space}
Let $S = \mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$ with $\deg(T_i) = 1$.
The scheme
$$
\mathbf{P}^n_{\mathbf{Z}} = \text{Proj}(S)
$$
represents the functor which associates to a scheme $Y$ the pairs
$(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots, s_n))$ where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module, and
\item $s_0, \ldots, s_n$ are global sections of $\mathcal{L}$
which generate $\mathcal{L}$
\end{enumerate}
up to the following equivalence:
$(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots, s_n)) \sim
(\mathcal{N}, (t_0, \ldots, t_n))$ $\Leftrightarrow$ there exists
an isomorphism $\beta : \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{N}$
with $\beta(s_i) = t_i$ for $i = 0, \ldots, n$.
stage_b_review_note: Source 2784–2803 identifies P^n_Z=Proj Z[T_0,..,T_n] with the functor of pairs consisting of a line bundle L over arbitrary scheme Y and n+1 global sections GENERATING L, modulo line-bundle isomorphisms carrying each section to its partner. The prepared claim preserves the moduli quotient.

stage_b_review_note: Pinned 2888–2899 enumerates four properties of P^n_S→S for every base scheme S: separatedness, quasi-compactness, existence and uniqueness of valuative extensions, and universal closedness. Stage A preserves all four, not merely properness as a compressed label.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
The structure morphism $\mathbf{P}^n_S \to S$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item separated,
\item quasi-compact,
\item satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion,
and
\item universally closed.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
The structure morphism $\mathbf{P}^n_S \to S$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item separated,
\item quasi-compact,
\item satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion,
and
\item universally closed.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-segre-embedding}
Let $S$ be a scheme. There exists a closed immersion
$$
\mathbf{P}^n_S \times_S \mathbf{P}^m_S
\longrightarrow
\mathbf{P}^{nm + n + m}_S
$$
called the {\it Segre embedding}.
stage_b_review_note: The original Segre lemma 2926–2935 asserts for a base scheme S a CLOSED immersion P^n_S×_S P^m_S→P^{nm+n+m}_S. Stage A's dimension nm+n+m = (n+1)(m+1)-1 and product over S agree exactly with the pinned source.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-in-projective-space}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $Z \subset \mathbf{P}^n_R$ be a closed subscheme.
Let
$$
I_d = \Ker\left(
R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]_d
\longrightarrow
\Gamma(Z, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^n_R}(d)|_Z)\right)
$$
Then $I = \bigoplus I_d \subset R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]$ is
a graded ideal and $Z = \text{Proj}(R[T_0, \ldots, T_n]/I)$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned 2988–3000 defines I_d as the kernel of degree-d polynomial global sections restricted to a closed Z⊂P^n_R and identifies Z with Proj of the graded quotient by ⊕I_d. Stage A preserves the graded kernel ideal and the identification, with no extra reducedness assertion.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-globally-generated-omega-twist-1}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible sheaf
and let $s_0, \ldots, s_n$ be global sections of $\mathcal{L}$
which generate it. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the kernel of the induced
map $\mathcal{O}_X^{\oplus n + 1} \to \mathcal{L}$.
Then $\mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}$ is globally generated.
stage_b_review_note: At 3153–3160, X is any scheme, L invertible and generated by global s_0,...,s_n, F=ker(O_X^{n+1}→L). The conclusion is global generation of F⊗L, not that F itself is globally generated. Stage A retains this twist and the kernel's definition.
